items.summary: Decompose html_website and publish monolith files

members.summary: generate_module_website() is a 400-line god function mixing HTML construction, JavaScript embedding, and per-question-type dispatch
publish/utils.py is a pipeline catch-all mixing flattening, cleaning, four copy operations, and category reorganization
legacy_import/main.py duplicates the chapter-map/copy/log pattern for full-slides and notes-slides within a single function
format_conversion is documented as a composition layer but bypassed entirely by the main pipeline, making its role invisible
canvas_integration.sync_module_structure is a public API stub that delegates entirely to upload_module_to_canvas with no distinct behavior
log_style.py is a fourth file type in batch_processing that breaks the package's own main/utils/config structural convention
185-line JavaScript block embedded as raw string literal inside a Python function body
Matching question validation always returns isCorrect=true with a comment acknowledging it is a placeholder
generate_module_website() is a 400-line function accumulating HTML state through mutable string concatenation with no intermediate helpers
create_questions_directory() in legacy_import/utils.py embeds 100+ lines of README.md and AGENTS.md template strings in function body
publish_all.py silently skips slides when --skip-copy-extras is used, because step 6 shares step 5's gate with no independent flag
format_conversion/main.py uses a string-keyed if/elif dispatch rather than a data-driven dispatch table
batch_processing/__init__.py re-exports the full internal API (18 symbols), eliminating package encapsulation
publish/utils.py is a 593-line multi-concern file mixing flatten, copy, reorganize, and clean operations across 7 distinct operation families

action_steps.detail: Extract the 185-line embedded JS string literal from html_website/main.py into a separate file alongside the main module, loaded via Path.read_text() at runtime

action_steps.detail: Split generate_module_website() into: _build_header_section(), _build_question_section(), _build_nav_section(), _build_lab_section(). Max 60 lines each.

action_steps.title: Split publish/utils.py into sub-modules by operation family (flatten, copy_labs, copy_slides, reorganize)
action_steps.detail: Split publish/utils.py into: publish/flatten.py, publish/copy_extras.py, publish/reorganize.py. Update publish/__init__.py to re-export.

items.summary: Fix broken logging initialization and module-scope side effects

members.summary: Module-scope get_logger() calls in src modules silently return unconfigured loggers if imported before setup_logging() is called
Half of src modules log to __name__ namespaces not under 'batch_processing', silently bypassing the file handler configured by setup_logging()
setup_logging() called at module scope in scripts creates a timestamped log file on disk as an import-time side effect
get_logger() silently returns an unconfigured logger if called before setup_logging(), with no documented ordering requirement
Lazy function-body imports in legacy_import/main.py indicate latent circular dependency pressure in the import graph

action_steps.title: Move setup_logging call out of module scope in generate_all_outputs.py and import_legacy_materials.py
action_steps.detail: In generate_all_outputs.py and import_legacy_materials.py move setup_logging() call inside if __name__ == '__main__' guard

action_steps.title: Fix logger hierarchy so batch_processing, publish, validation, legacy_import all log to configured handler
action_steps.detail: In setup_logging() use logging.getLogger() (root logger) or configure each module logger: src.publish, src.validation, src.legacy_import, src.batch_processing

action_steps.title: Audit all getLogger calls for correct hierarchy
action_steps.detail: Audit all getLogger(__name__) calls. Ensure hierarchy aligns with setup_logging config. Convert deferred imports to top-level in batch_processing.

items.summary: Fix silent errors and inconsistent error handling patterns

members.summary: Silent bare except in html_website/main.py swallows question-parsing errors with no logging
validate_outputs(), generate_validation_report(), and _validate_module_outputs() annotate formats as List[str] but the parameter accepts None
canvas_integration/main.py upload_module_to_canvas() broad except clause hides error contract from callers
batch_render_lab_manuals() silently swallows per-file errors, returning partial results with no indication of failure count
html_website/main.py silently swallows JSON parse errors for questions file with bare `except Exception: pass`

process_module_to_pdf, process_module_to_audio, process_module_to_text in batch_processing use print() for errors while process_module_by_type uses logger.error — inconsistent error output within the same file
canvas_integration _upload_file_to_canvas() uses requests.post() directly for the upload step, bypassing the make_canvas_request() wrapper and its rate-limiting protection
batch_processing/utils.py get_courses_to_process() returns List[tuple] — the inner tuple type is undeclared
publish/utils.py copy_directory_contents logs errors but returns a potentially low count with no indication of partial failure to callers
canvas_integration uses a Result-accumulator dict error strategy while all other modules use raise-or-print — strategy is isolated to one module without documentation
file_validation/main.py check_file_sizes silently skips unreadable files with no log

action_steps.detail: In canvas_integration/main.py upload_module_to_canvas replace broad except with specific exceptions. Accumulate errors, return with error list in result dict.

action_steps.detail: In batch_render_lab_manuals return (results, errors) tuple or add 'failed_count' key to result dict. Fix copy_directory_contents to return (count, errors).

action_steps.detail: Align generate_module_renderings.py to use logger.info/error instead of print(). Import the same logger as generate_all_outputs.py uses.

items.summary: Fix API shape inconsistencies and pure delegations

members.summary: sync_module_structure is a documented public function that only forwards to upload_module_to_canvas with a renamed parameter
process_module_website takes one path argument while all sibling process_module_to_* functions take two (module_path + output_dir)
process_* functions at the batch_processing boundary return inconsistently shaped dicts requiring callers to know internal structure
process_module_by_type and process_course_* family functions lack Raises documentation despite calling converters that raise ValueError/OSError
sync_module_structure() copies the ValueError/RequestException raise contract but only delegates to upload_module_to_canvas() without adding any new raises
canvas_integration/main.py inspects raw validation dict from file_validation inline instead of translating at one boundary point
html_website/main.py and batch_processing functions accept str paths at public API boundary requiring immediate internal conversion to Path

action_steps.detail: Add output_dir: Optional[Path] = None parameter to process_module_website() to match process_module_to_pdf/docx/etc sibling signatures

action_steps.title: Either add policy to sync_module_structure or remove it and update callers
action_steps.detail: Remove sync_module_structure() and update callers to call upload_module_to_canvas() directly, OR add real policy (validation, logging, retry) to justify its existence

action_steps.title: Align process_* result dict schemas across modules and batch_render_lab_manuals
action_steps.detail: Standardize process_* result dicts: modules use {summary:{...}} nested, labs use flat {files:[...]}. Define ProcessResult TypedDict and use everywhere.

items.summary: Fix cross-module architecture: hub modules, deferred imports, boundaries

members.summary: batch_processing/main.py uses deferred function-level imports for all cross-module calls, hiding runtime dependencies from static analysis
format_conversion module duplicates markdown_to_pdf module's core responsibility with no documented boundary rationale
publish/utils.py is a cross-cutting megafile absorbing flattening, copying, reorganization, and publication concerns
html_website couples to batch_processing logging infrastructure rather than a shared logging utility
batch_processing re-exports 15+ symbols from downstream converters, acting as a God package that collapses architectural layers
batch_processing/utils.py imports from module_organization creating a lateral Layer 0 dependency
scripts/flatten_published.py is a redundant entry point after its logic was migrated to publish/utils.py, which publish_all.py already calls

action_steps.title: Convert deferred imports in batch_processing to top-level
action_steps.detail: In batch_processing/main.py move all function-level imports to top of file. If cycles emerge, that reveals real architectural issues to fix.

action_steps.title: Reduce batch_processing re-export surface
action_steps.detail: In batch_processing/__init__.py reduce re-exports to only the public API functions needed by external callers. Remove internal helpers.

action_steps.title: Move format_conversion to use proper composition layer
action_steps.detail: Ensure format_conversion is the composition layer for all PDF/DOCX/audio generation. Remove direct lower-level calls from batch_processing bypassing format_conversion.
